newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU members told to clean up act on single market.
newsitem.headline: EU members told to clean up act on single market.

text.p: The European Union will not feel the promised benefits of the bloc's border-free market on job creation and growth unless members clean up their act and apply the laws properly, the European Commission said on Thursday.

The EU executive said ahead of a meeting of internal trade ministers in Luxembourg on Friday that EU members had made almost no progress since May in adopting legislation necessary to make the market work.

"The single market cannot deliver its full benefits in terms of job creation, economic growth or competitiveness unless member states improve their record on applying single market rules on the ground," it said in a statement.
It said Mario Monti, the Commissioner responsible for the single market, would threaten at the meeting to take legal action against EU countries which did not comply.

"Mr Monti will tell the ministers that on the basis of the information verified so far, there has been little substantial progress on the general state of implementation of single market directives," the statement said.

Minister will be presented with figures showing that EU states have adopted in national legislation only 93.3 percent of the 219 measures included in the EU's single market programme, against 92.6 percent in May.
The Commission said that even where members seemed to have implemented the measures, they had often done so in an unsatisfactory way.
Particular problem areas concerned legislation intended to create open markets in the bloc for insurance services and public contracts.
The Commission said that only three EU countries -- Denmark, Luxembourg and the Netherlands -- have fully implemented all the legislation intended to create a 15-nation zone for public contracts.
It said it had taken legal action against member states in 39 cases. Greece and Spain had failed to implement the EU's insurance legislation, it said.
The Commission said that in 1996 it had sent 128 warning letters, opened second-stage infringement proceedings in 56 cases and referred 11 cases to the European Court of Justice.

Monti will remind member states that if they fail to apply EU legislation they risk facing claims for damages from aggrieved EU businesses and citizens, following an October 8 European Court ruling, the statement said.
